One host already does seven shows right now, so the schedule itself is impossible.

lines.trans: When one person agrees, the other dislikes them, and when the other agrees, this one backs out.
Getting someone who says no to say yes is what casting is all about.
If everyone said yes right away, why would anyone need casting?
This is just like dating. You need the right amount of push and pull.
Then you should handle it yourself, Producer.
After all, you are so good at dating.
Fine, I will do it! Our team is in an emergency right now.

보다.gloss: to see, to watch; to take (an exam)

meanings.en: to see, to look at, to watch
meanings.note: Primary meaning.
Idiomatic in 시험을 보다.

examples.trans: I watched a movie on the weekend.
I took the driver's license exam.

meanings.note: 1st person plural pronoun; also used for 'my' with family, school, or workplace

examples.trans: Our team has a good atmosphere.
Let's eat lunch together tomorrow.

meanings.note: Interrogative adverb.

examples.trans: Why are you running?

meanings.note: General-purpose counter noun used with native Korean determiners (한 개, 두 개, 세 개).

examples.trans: How many do you need?

meanings.en: to do, to perform, to hold
meanings.note: Core verb; also combines with nouns to form verbs.

We are holding a meeting today.
Did you hear about this schedule?
I was busy today because of schedule.

없다.gloss: to not exist, to not have

examples.trans: I don't have time right now.

meanings.note: Can refer to a single person or people/a crowd in general without a plural suffix.

meanings.note: Humble first-person singular pronoun used in polite speech.

examples.trans: I have an induction ceremony.

meanings.note: Descriptive verb (adjective); the thing disliked takes the subject marker 이/가.
